limitations: This is an offline design and tool review. It is not product acceptance, not product Gate 0, not a Stage PASS and not a human signature.
The product coordinate stays R1 / WAIT_HUMAN; the 621b1bf experience signature is still absent; the samples stay NOT_MATERIALIZED_NOT_FROZEN and the MS cases, the V1-M1 stage and R22 stay NOT_RUN.
The checker validates plan and contract STRUCTURE. It never runs product code, never opens the product database, never produces a runtime ETag header and never materializes a sample.

The candidate migration SQL was parsed as text only and never executed. The DDL that defines lvw_scene_hash is not part of the frozen package, so the scene hash could only be verified against the declared prose rule, never against a shipped function.

The NM-6 conclusion is an offline declaration conformance result. No runtime adapter exists in this package, so it proves that the declared rule is implementable and unambiguous; it does not verify product output.
The effective OpenAPI was replayed in memory by the reviewer's own code; no effective OpenAPI document was generated or shipped.

jsonschema 4.23.0 was importable in this environment and the full metaschema check and the retained-frame instance probe therefore ran. On a host without jsonschema the checker degrades, and the degradation is now disclosed in the run output (probes P25 and P26). No validation was omitted in the candidate run, and no omitted validation is reported as a product PASS.
The implementation's provider and model identity is self-reported and was not independently verified.

The supplementary verify_pack count differs by one from the candidate's hash-bound log (7531 against 7530 on the reconstructed candidate tree); the cause is the MANIFEST.sha256 line count that the receipt itself states, and the bound log remains the authority for the figure it carries. The historical 7475 figure is unaffected.
The 23 probes are a bounded independent selection, not an exhaustive enumeration of every input the checker accepts; the reviewer does not claim the remaining untested inputs are clean.

The shape handler behind the checks covers AttributeError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError, ValueError and re.error; an exception of another class would still escape as a traceback. The run stays fail-closed on the exit code.
